messages:
incident-bot: Pager: High error rate + degraded latency on serving-runtime (us-west-2). 30% 5xx, many containers restarting. Paging on-call. priority: P1

alex_s: I'm on it. seeing lots of pod restarts in r-runtime-serve namespace. Crashloop backoffs.

maria_ml: logs show repeated `CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY` from nvcruntime in model-worker. Also a few `failed to allocate device memory` traces.

dmitri: link to kube events: http://k8s-logs/cluster/us-west-2/events?query=runtime-serve - nodes are flapping between NotReady and Ready. Something's killing the pods while new nodes spin up.

laura_pm: Customer-impact: multiple customers on dedicated capacity reporting > 500ms tail latency, some 5xx. CS is seeing escalation in the queue. @cust-success prepping comms.

cust-success: FYI filing incident page for affected customers, starting with legacy-embed-prod and chat-realtime. We'll send initial "investigating" soon.

alex_s: Hypothesis: cluster-autoscaler overscaling then quickly removing nodes -> GPUs fail to initialize or driver mismatch -> worker OOMs during warmup -> crashloops. Saw pattern: scaleup -> new pods schedule -> init logs show driver probe warnings -> pod OOMs -> CA drains node -> repeat.

srebot: autoscaler events: 12 scale-up events in 10m, 9 scale-downs within 3m after scale-up. Scaleup size: +8 GPUs, then -7.

maria_ml: stack snippet from pod stderr:
```
2026-03-15T14:02:13Z model-worker[pid]: cuda runtime: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY: out of memory when allocating 4096MiB
2026-03-15T14:02:13Z model-worker[pid]: attempt retry -> reinit attempt 2
2026-03-15T14:02:14Z model-worker[pid]: gpu driver probe warning: mismatch kernel module version
```

dmitri: Also seeing Kubelet kubelet: evicting pod due to node pressure, but node reports <10% memory used. suspicion: GPU memory accounting mismatch causing pods to think no GPU available.

alex_s: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) pause cluster-autoscaler 2) pin desired node count to stable capacity for the moment 3) prevent new deployments of the new quantized model variant 4) scale down model replica concurrency/batch size to reduce footprint.

ops-bot: Running: `kubectl annotate deployment cluster-autoscaler cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/paused=true --overwrite -n kube-system` (requires SRE perms).

laura_pm: @alex_s do we need to revert the recent model rollout? It started ~14:00 UTC and coincides with spike.

maria_ml: Yes that rollout pushed a new quantized checkpoint and a container image with different CUDA toolkit. Could be causing driver/API mismatches. Recommend pinning to stable image.

alex_s: Rolling back the model rollout now: `kubectl set image deploy/model-service model=model-service:v2026-03-14-stable -n runtime-serve`

srebot: rollback started, new pods scheduling.

dmitri: Also setting cluster-autoscaler flag: `--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m --max-node-provision-time=20m` temporarily to reduce thrash. Applied via helm values patch.

ops-bot: Helm upgrade command executed with new CA values. Confirmed CA not removing nodes in last 2m.

maria_ml: For immediate pod stability, setting env override `MODEL_MAX_BATCH=1` and `KV_CACHE=false` on model workers to reduce peak GPU memory.

alex_s: Patching deployments with the env override.

cust-success: Sending update to impacted customers: "We're investigating degraded performance in us-west-2, engineers are mitigating. We'll follow up with root cause and ETA."

laura_pm: Any sign of reduced crashloops?

srebot: Crashloop count decreased from 118 to 12 in the last 6 minutes. Latency p50/p95 improving but still elevated.

dmitri: Observed another class of errors on the new nodes: `nvidia-driver: failed module init` — looks like AMI/driver install race during node bootstrap. New nodes come up but driver install finishes after pods request GPU -> init fails.

maria_ml: Longer-term: should add node-init hook to wait for nvidia modules or use a pre-baked AMI with locked driver. Also update admission controller to refuse GPU-allocating pods until driver ready.

alex_s: For now: 1) cordon the freshest nodes that still report driver issues 2) replace them with pre-baked AMI nodes from stable pool 3) keep CA paused until stable for 30m.

ops-bot: `kubectl cordon ip-10-0-4-52.us-west-2` -> cordoned. `eksctl create nodegroup --node-ami=ami-stable-202602 --nodes 4` requested.

dmitri: Also turning off HPA on model-service to prevent aggressive horizontal spin-up: `kubectl scale hpa model-service --replicas=4 -n runtime-serve` then annotate to disable reconcilers.

laura_pm: CS reports some customers already seeing degraded but stable connectivity. We'll track escalation. Any ETA to fully restore?

alex_s: If rollback + pause CA + env overrides hold, expect steady state in ~20-30m. Full remediation (AMI + driver) will take 2-3 hours.

srebot: Metrics: 5xx rate down from 30% to 6% over 12 minutes after rollback and CA pause. Token cost spikes noted due to retries; cost team looped in.

maria_ml: Recording follow-ups: - bake AMI with tested driver (owner: eng-infra) - add nodeReady GPU annotation gating (owner: eng-runtime) - add CA scale guard for rapid oscillation (owner: eng-platform) - postmortem (owner: laura_pm).

cust-success: Sending second update: "Mitigations in place, error rate significantly reduced. We're continuing to monitor and will provide a full report."

alex_s: On-call handoff in 45m to @dmitri for ongoing monitoring. If any regression, page SRE.

laura_pm: Creating incident doc and assigning follow-ups. Thanks team. :thumbsup: 

incident-bot: Incident transitioned to "mitigated" state at 2026-03-15T15:14:59Z. Postmortem scheduled for 2026-03-16 16:00 UTC.
